item.title: MPCB asks Adani firm to stop work on temporary labour camp in Satara
item.description: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to stop excavation and construction work for its temporary camp in Satara district for allegedly beginning these without obtaining the necessary environmental clearance and permissions. The labour camp in Satara's Patan taluka, some 300 kilometres from here, is part of the firm's 1500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a stop-work notice dated November 20, the MPCB said the company had started excavation and development work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawargahar village for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities without informing the board or obtaining the required permissions. The company had not secured environmental clearance for the excavation and development work from the competent authority, the MPCB added. The notice, issued under Section 33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Section 31A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act .

item.title: ITC extends Braille-enabled packaging to Fiama, takes total to 16 SKUs
item.description: Alongside an industry-wide shift toward AI-enabled personalisation and algorithmic optimisation, diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd is pursuing an analogue, inclusive approach to product innovation by incorporating raised Braille text on select personal care items from its Savlon and Fiama portfolios. The initiative makes everyday consumer products more accessible to millions of visually impaired people in India, for whom routine activities such as identifying a handwash bottle or choosing the right personal care product can pose challenges. Building on Savlon's introduction of India's first Braille-enabled FMCG packaging in 2018, ITC's Personal Care Products Business has now extended the initiative to Fiama. It now has 16 SKUs from the personal care segment under accessible packaging. Braille identifiers are currently featured on technically feasible product packs, such as Savlon Antiseptic Disinfectant Liquid, Savlon Wet Wipes and Handwash Pumps, as well as Fiama Shower Gels. item.title: Shree Cement to cross 100 MT capacity in 3-4 yrs, targets 9-10% growth
item.description: Shree Cement, the country's third-largest cement maker by installed capacity, is expecting to cross the 100 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) production capacity over the next three to four years, driven by an aggressive expansion push and steady demand from the country's infrastructure and housing sectors, said its Chairman Hari Mohan Bangur. In an interaction with PTI, Bangur said the company is targeting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9-10 per cent over the next six to seven years, higher than the expected 7-8 per cent growth in the overall Indian cement industry. Shree Cement Ltd (SCL), which earlier this month announced a Rs 7,000 crore investment to set up cement plants in Andhra Pradesh as part of its expansion, expects to reach 80 MTPA capacity in the next two years, he said. item.description: Global hospitality platform Airbnb is looking to deepen its presence in India by expanding beyond traditional holiday destinations, strengthening the homestay ecosystem and bringing more local entrepreneurs onto its platform to tap the country's growing domestic travel market. item.title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
item.description: Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said. The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said. "It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.
